Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Apex CyberSecure Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star then one on your telephone keypad if you would like to ask a question. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex CyberSecure's results for the third quarter of fiscal 2024. With me on today's call are Jordan Hayes, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Kline, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Mark Thornton, Chief Security Officer; Lisa Chen, VP of Sales; David Patel, Chief Marketing Officer; and Rachel Kim, Chief Product Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jordan Hayes.

Jordan Hayes: Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. Apex CyberSecure delivered exceptional results in the third quarter, exceeding expectations across all key metrics. Our performance reflects the strength of our product portfolio, our expanding customer base, and our commitment to innovation. The adoption rate of FalconX is accelerating, demonstrating its powerful impact in slashing mean time to detect and respond to threats while delivering unmatched value to our customers.

Our strategic priorities are focused on eight key areas: strengthening customer feedback loops on our new products and features, advancing market share trends across core segments, ramping up R&D investment as a percentage of revenue, clarifying assumptions underlying our guidance, sustaining our Net Dollar Retention rate, expanding the number of customers with ARR over $100K, boosting channel partner performance and their revenue contribution, and accelerating platform adoption rates versus point products.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Kline to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Sarah Kline: Thank you, Jordan. We achieved record revenue of $720 million in the third quarter, representing a 32% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin remained strong at 87%, and we continued to invest aggressively in growth initiatives. Operating expenses were $480 million. Net income was $160 million, resulting in earnings per share of $0.92. We are increasing our full-year revenue guidance to $2.85 billion to $2.95 billion and earnings guidance accordingly, based on our strong performance to date.

As we dive deeper into these results, let me highlight one of our strongest performance drivers: customer feedback on our new products and features. This goes far beyond anecdotal praise—it's supported by solid metrics from Net Promoter Score surveys, Customer Satisfaction data, and insights from our Global Customer Advisory Board, featuring CISOs from Fortune 500 enterprises in financial services, healthcare, and critical infrastructure. Our overall NPS for new product adoption reached 78 in Q3, up 13 points year-over-year and 22 points from Q1 2024, placing us in the top quartile of the IDC Cybersecurity Customer Experience Index—ahead of peers like Palo Alto Networks and close to CrowdStrike's 82. CSAT for latest releases hit 92%, with 87% of respondents saying our AI-driven features exceeded expectations. Churn among new-feature adopters was just 1.2% annualized, well below Gartner's 8-10% industry average for EDR platforms.

Our FalconX Next-Gen EDR platform, launched in Q2 with hyper-scale behavioral analytics via our proprietary Graph Neural Network engine, has been a standout. Customers saw a 35% average reduction in mean time to detect and respond to advanced persistent threats, confirmed in joint proof-of-concepts with over 1,200 accounts. They love the zero-trust segmentation that integrates with MITRE ATT&CK frameworks—92% cited it as a key edge over Microsoft's Defender or Symantec Endpoint Security. A major U.S. financial institution reported 42% less alert fatigue, freeing SOC teams for true high-fidelity incidents.

Our Cloud Native Application Protection Platform, enhanced with Kubernetes-native runtime security, earned high marks from DevSecOps teams. In surveys of 450 multi-cloud customers on AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud, 95% praised auto-remediation workflows using our ML-based risk prioritization against CVSS 4.0 standards. This drove a 28% upsell rate in Q3, adding $47 million to cloud security ARR, up 62% year-over-year. In APAC, with 40% quarter-over-quarter growth in bookings, feedback stresses compliance with regs like Singapore's PDPA and Australia's Privacy Act updates—a Sydney telco noted 51% less cloud misconfiguration drift amid supply chain attacks like SolarWinds.

Our Secure Access Service Edge portfolio's Zero Trust Network Access 2.0 update, with inline deep packet inspection and SWG-as-a-Service, transformed remote work security. NPS here is 85, thanks to 30% better user experience than VPNs. From 650 enterprises, 76% blocked 99.7% of phishing via sandbox-integrated URL filtering, matching Zscaler's performance but with under 50ms global latency. Integration with ServiceNow for automated ticketing helped an EMEA healthcare provider contain breaches 25% faster.

Regionally, North America at 55% of revenue shows 91% adoption of Ransomware Shield using polymorphic decoys against LockBit and BlackCat, amid 28% ransomware surge per Chainalysis—NPS 81, upsell ACV up 22%. EMEA's DLP suite for GDPR and NIS2 hit 94% CSAT post-Okta learnings, winning 15 DAX 40 bank deals over Proofpoint. APAC loves our Quantum-Resistant Crypto preview in Identity Platform, with 89% satisfaction; Japan's edge SWG cuts data sovereignty risks.

Customer input shapes our roadmap—we're doubling down on GenAI security with AI Guardian detecting prompt injection in LLMs like GPT-4, in beta with 200 adopters for 40% fewer shadow AI risks. UTM API integrations with Splunk, Elastic, Sumo Logic have 96% success. Our data lake on 10 trillion daily events shows 150% rise in identity attacks, backing passwordless MFA with FIDO2. This validates platformization: 68% use 4+ modules, driving 145% net retention per Bessemer. We're putting $250 million into FY25 R&D for autonomous SOC, per CISO roundtables. Supply chain risks post-MoveIt are mitigated with 9.2/10 SBOM transparency.

This feedback fuels 32% growth and $4.2 billion ARR run-rate. Q4 betas include homomorphic encryption.

Transitioning seamlessly, market share trends continue to solidify our leadership. The global cybersecurity market grew 12.3% to $62 billion in H1 2024 per IDC, driven by 28% ransomware surge and AI attacks. Our TAM in EDR, SASE, CWPP expands at 18-20% CAGR to 2027 per Gartner. In EDR/next-gen AV, we hold 14.2% share, up from 11.8% YoY—a 20% gain outpacing 15% segment growth. In SASE via ApexEdge ZTNA/SWG, 8.7% share, doubled from 4.1%, ahead of Symantec's 6.2% and near Zscaler's 9.1%.

In EDR, ApexSentinel agentless sensor with GNN drove 35% ARR growth to $1.2 billion, 42% net new logos, 18% ACV to $450K. Share at 16.5%, displacing CrowdStrike in 22% win-backs via Azure Sentinel/AWS Security Hub integrations. ApexSentinel 7.2's federated learning cut MTTD 47%. In CWPP, 28% share gain with ApexCloudGuard eBPF inspection, 11.3% share over Check Point's 9.8%, NRR 128%.

North America at 62% revenue holds 18.4% EDR share with $150M DoD CMMC win. EMEA 22% revenue grew 31% to 12.1% share on NIS2; APAC 55% growth to 10% revenue, 7.2% share in Japan/ANZ via NTT/Telstra. Landmark €80M Big Four bank deal. LatAm/MEA 6% revenue up 40%, targeting 10% share.

We win 68% vs. CrowdStrike, 72% vs. SentinelOne, 55% vs. Palo Alto on TCO and ApexAI autonomy. Legacy like Trend Micro down 15-20%. $2.1B cash funds DeepTrace AI acquisition, 22% R&D. NVIDIA/ServiceNow partnerships ahead. Churn sub-2%, 95% gross retention. FY25 guide 25-28% growth, 2-3 share points to 16%.

Next, our R&D investment hit $148 million in Q3, or 22.4% of $661 million revenue base—up 180bps from 20.6% on $512 million last year. Nine months at 21.8% vs. 19.7%. Non-GAAP op margin 28%, gross 85%+ on SaaS. Peers: CrowdStrike 23%, Palo Alto 18-19%, Zscaler 22%. Headcount +12% to 1,850 via AI workflows.

Key areas: 45% to Nexus Sentinel XDR with eBPF zero-trust, MTTR under 5 mins vs. Emotet. 20% quantum-resistant Kyber/Dilithium in SASE for 'Harvest Now' threats, 30% latency wins. 18% GenAI Huntly Labs for MITRE playbooks vs. 300% phishing surge. 17% edge/IoT Rust agents for OT.

Regions: NA 60%, EMEA 22% up on NIS2 DLP, APAC 18% +35% vs. Salt Typhoon. Industry R&D up to 21% per Gartner; our 1:3.2 patent ratio, 47 Q3 filings. FY24 21-23%, FY25 +$50M sovereign clouds. Drives 4x NRR, 125% retention.

On NDR, we hit 118% for Q3—11th quarter over 115%, +300bps sequential, +620bps YoY vs. peer 112%. Starting ARR cohort grew to $118 per $100. Gross retention 96%, churn <2% via ML health scoring. Net expansion 122%, up 15% QoQ.

Drivers: CyberShield Sentinel 2.0 GenAI SOAR $45M expansions; Zero Trust Edge + Cisco Meraki 18% ACV; compliance packs NIST/DORA/SEC $28M. NA 120%, EMEA 116% Paris region, APAC 112% IRAP/PDPA. $50M Land-and-Expand pods, 75% 4+ modules vs. CrowdStrike 65%. Q4 to 120% with Quantum suite.

High-value customers with >$100K ARR ended at 512, +18% sequential, +42% YoY from 361. 68% total ARR. +92 net new, 15 Fortune 500 equivs—top-5 bank SASE, EU healthcare EDR. Win rate 28% vs. incumbents, ShieldAI MTTD -65%. Cohort NRR 128%, 73% 3+ modules, avg ARR $245K +14%.

Regions: Americas 368 +22% SEC rules; EMEA 92 +55% DORA/NIS2; APAC 52 +38% Snowflake DSPM. ShieldAI automates 85% SOC, quantum modules. 31% multi-year, 38mo duration. Q4 +110-130 new.

Channels: 65% revenue $468M +28% YoY from $182M last? Wait, total $720M so adjust: 65% $468M, +28% YoY. ARR $1.2B of $2.1B total, partner NRR 118%. Elite Optiv/CDW 42% $197M avg $1.8M TCV. MSPs 32% $150M +35%, MDR $420M ARR 82% margins. Dists 26% $121M.

Americas 72% $337M +32% CISA ZTNA; EMEA 18% $84M +42% NIS2 DORA OT; APAC 10% $47M +25% AWS. Subs 92%, partner-led 55%, multi-prod +30%. PartnerForge 3.0 AI portal trained 4,200, 40% close lift, $65M hyperscaler pipeline. FY24 70%+ channel, $850M partner ARR.

Finally, platform adoption: SecureNet One 78% ARR $1.42B +52% YoY vs. point 12% $412M. New ACV $1.8M vs $320K 5.6x. 90% enterprise platform-only. Gartner: point sprawl 47% fatigue, our 68% MTTR cut. Platform NER 128% +$240K ARR/customer, churn 3.2% vs 11%. 65% expansions from point footholds.

NA 85% bookings AWS/Azure CNAPP; EMEA 42% growth EU sovereignty 17>$10M; APAC 72% +61% Japan $45M auto. Nexus 3.0 GenAI 92% accuracy 40% OpEx save; Fabric multi-cloud ServiceNow; 450 ISVs. Platform GM 89% vs 76%. YE24 80-82%, 12% DBNR +300bps, 1,200 $1M+ customers +45%. $2.1B expansions.

These metrics underpin our raised guidance.

Dr. Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Sarah. Our technology team is focused on developing cutting-edge security solutions that leverage the latest advancements in artificial intelligence, machine learning, and cloud computing. Key areas of focus include ramping R&D investments to pioneer next-gen XDR, quantum-resistant crypto, and GenAI threat hunting, ensuring we stay ahead of evolving threats.

Mark Thornton: Security remains our top priority. We are continuously monitoring the threat landscape—from ransomware variants to state-sponsored APTs—and adapting our security posture to protect our customers and our own infrastructure with zero-trust principles and real-time intelligence.

Lisa Chen: We are seeing strong demand for our solutions across all geographies and industry verticals. Our sales team is focused on building strong relationships with customers and partners, expanding market share through land-and-expand motions and channel acceleration.

David Patel: Our marketing efforts are focused on building brand awareness and generating demand through digital channels, PR, events, and thought leadership, positioning Apex CyberSecure as a trusted advisor in cybersecurity.

Rachel Kim: Our product strategy centers on innovative, integrated solutions addressing customer needs. We gather ongoing feedback to refine our platform, ensuring it exceeds expectations in a rapidly changing threat environment.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: Thank you. Instructions for Q&A: If you are using a speakerphone, please pick up your handset before pressing the keys. Limit to one question and one follow-up. First question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith: Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Can you expand on customer feedback for the new FalconX features and how that's influencing the roadmap?

Jordan Hayes: Thanks, John. Absolutely, customer feedback has been phenomenal, as Sarah detailed—NPS at 78, CSAT 92%, with standout wins on MTTD reductions and integrations. It's directly accelerating our GenAI and quantum initiatives for Q4 betas. We're listening closely to CISOs on platform expansions.

Operator: Next question comes from Maria Lopez with Morgan Stanley.

Maria Lopez: Great results. On guidance, what are the key assumptions, especially around macro and regional growth?

Sarah Kline: Thanks, Maria. Our FY25 guidance of $2.85B-$2.95B revenue assumes 12-14% market growth per Gartner, with buffers for rates at 4-4.5%, no recession, 5% FX headwind. Segment-wise, 35% cloud, 20% endpoint; NA 20-25%, EMEA 22%, APAC 25-30%. RPO 1.5x coverage, conservative on pipelines and churn under 4%.

Operator: Next question comes from Raj Patel with Barclays.

Raj Patel: Solid NDR and R&D spend. Thoughts on tech roadmap for AI and quantum?

Dr. Elena Vasquez: Thanks, Raj. Our 22% R&D intensity funds Sentinel XDR autonomy, Kyber crypto in SASE, GenAI playbooks—MTTR under 5 mins. Regional tilts like APAC for threats, with patents flowing. Ties to 118% NDR via expansions.

Operator: Next question comes from Emily Grant with JPMorgan.

Emily Grant: On channel strength and platform vs. point, any competitive insights?

Mark Thornton: Thanks, Emily. Channels at 65% revenue with 118% partner NRR, Elite partners driving $1.8M deals. Platform at 78% ARR, 89% margins, gaining on Zscaler/Palo Alto via unified Nexus—churn 3.2% vs. 11% point. Secures us against breaches averaging $4.88M.

Jordan Hayes: Thank you for your insightful questions. We are confident in our ability to continue to deliver strong results and create value for our shareholders. Thank you to our employees, customers, and partners.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
